# Native global-shortcut ownership

The immutable reference is Mluva v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. [The independent fixture](released-shortcuts.json), SHA-256 `3046a1d5cf42ae2231752d6fbbdae251f8144345b5c784ed8f9c484220db1ffe`, records 21 released service workflows and 59 event states. The temporary observer imports the unchanged release, calls its real `GlobalShortcutService`, and verifies every imported Mluva module against the pinned commit. It replaces no handler or transport. The collector stays under ignored `tmp/`; native verification uses no interpreter.

Both implementations contact the same separate [native portal peer](../../examples/global_shortcut_portal_peer.rs) over an actual private session bus. The peer imports no Mluva implementation. Its received method signatures, application identity, valid opaque tokens, proposed descriptions/keys, session ownership, explicit request/session closure and caller disconnects are compared with the released trace. Generated caller names and tokens are represented by per-workflow client numbers and independently checked ownership/format facts; shortcut IDs, key descriptions, errors and callback order remain exact. Control requests configure the external portal and emit real signals; the production owner has no test mode, injected transport or synthetic callback receipt.

The workflows cover F9 and F24 startup, invalid-key rejection, duplicate activation suppression until release, cancellation/latest actions, unknown IDs and foreign sessions, compositor-assigned triggers, missing/blank bindings, repeated start and unchanged keys. F9-to-F10 replacement and two key changes while approval is pending verify serialization and rejection of obsolete approval status. Responses before their method return, including an alternate request path belonging to the same caller, are preserved. Optional host-registration failure, cancelled/denied approval, missing/foreign handles, invalid replies, malformed shortcut lists/properties, controlled remote errors and compositor session closure remain recoverable. Pending CreateSession and BindShortcuts are explicitly closed, then their private connections disappear.

Review added a post-closure malformed activation that failed before the native owner required a real, still-owned session. An absent session and an invalid event field can no longer compare equal and trigger recording. The same guard covers binding changes. Two other independently reproduced differences are repaired: portal display keys use the released whitespace definition, and a dictionary cannot masquerade as an empty approved-shortcut list. The native owner also validates request object-path syntax before retaining it for cleanup; arbitrary remote error bodies are never surfaced.

Shutdown is terminal and acknowledged: it immediately suppresses application callbacks, closes outstanding approval/session handles, waits for queued replacements, and closes only its private connection. The released threaded service emits an internal “request was closed” error during the two pending-approval shutdowns; these are retained separately as `shutdown_notifications` in the fixture. Native checks intentionally require silence once shutdown starts, including later activation, start and key-change attempts. This is an explicit lifecycle strengthening, not a claim that those internal shutdown notifications are identical. Cleanup calls have bounded two-second reply waits.

Build the development peer, then run the ignored test explicitly in the existing guarded environment:

```sh
cargo build --locked -p mluva-gtk --example global_shortcut_portal_peer
bash dev/run-isolated-browser.sh tmp/shortcut-evidence -- \
  cargo test --locked -p mluva-gtk --test global_shortcuts -- --ignored --nocapture
```

The runner isolates HOME/XDG, display, session/accessibility buses, network/PID namespaces and devices. Both test and peer check those boundaries before acquiring the portal name. No host input, clipboard, portal, microphone, credentials or user content is used. Exclude the development peer from distribution.

The wire contract follows the official [GlobalShortcuts portal](https://flatpak.github.io/xdg-desktop-portal/docs/doc-org.freedesktop.portal.GlobalShortcuts.html) and [Request lifecycle](https://flatpak.github.io/xdg-desktop-portal/docs/doc-org.freedesktop.portal.Request.html), preserving the released CreateSession/BindShortcuts flow. This check proves the client protocol and service ownership against a controlled peer. It does not prove compositor approval UI, physical function keys, GNOME/Hyprland behavior, assembled-application key wiring, background startup, the shell helper/widget, screenshots or distribution. Those integration and complete-workflow acceptance rows remain Pending; the installed app/widget remain 1.6.0.
